transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice weekly during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. Before I can approve this, I need to gather relevant implementation information from each of you. Could the STEM teacher, school nurse, and technology coordinator each share what you know regarding the practical, safety, and technical considerations for this program?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important update from my room-safety review. I completed the review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be revised before the program can be safely authorized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share findings from my review of the participating students' health records. I found that one student has a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3

The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan.
